raw_response:
Well, I've been doing this wheat-maize rotation for decades on these 8 mu, and at my age I know this land better than my own hands. Let me think through this year carefully.

**Wheat** (planted last October, now in jointing):

My wheat is already in the ground — I put in Jimai 22 back in early October, about 12 kg seed per mu, and applied base fertilizer as compound 15-15-15 at around 40 kg/mu before planting. That gave me roughly 6 kg N, 6 kg P₂O₅, 6 kg K₂O from the base. Now in April, I'm at jointing stage. Based on how the crop looks — decent tillering, color is okay but could be greener in patches — I'm planning to topdress 15 kg urea per mu with my first spring irrigation. That's about 7 kg N. Total N comes to around 13 kg/mu, which is on the lower end but my soil has been built up over years of straw return, and I don't want to push it too hard at these fertilizer prices.

Irrigation: I'll do two this spring — one at jointing combined with the topdress, one at booting if May stays dry. Well water costs me about 20 yuan/mu per irrigation with the electric pump. Three would be safer but that's another 160 yuan I'd rather keep. If we get a decent rain in May I might skip the second.

I'll spray once for aphids and powdery mildew around heading — you always get some, and prevention is cheaper than letting it spread. Expected yield around 450 kg/mu — I've gotten 480-500 in good years, 400 in dry ones. This year looks average.

**Maize** (to plant mid-June after wheat harvest):

Tight turnaround — combine harvests wheat around June 8-12, then I have maybe 5 days to get maize in. I use no-till direct seeding through the wheat stubble; I pay the local service about 30 yuan/mu for the planter. Zhengdan 958 or a similar mid-late variety, around 4-5 kg seed per mu.

Apply compound fertilizer 25-10-8 at about 40 kg/mu at planting through the seeder, then topdress 20 kg urea at V6-V8 stage in late July. That's around 19 kg N total — maize is heavier feeding than wheat and summer rainfall leaches nitrogen, so I push harder here. Usually don't need to irrigate summer maize — July-August rains handle it — but I'll keep one irrigation in reserve if we hit a dry spell at tasseling.

One herbicide spray post-emergence (atrazine + acetochlor), and watch for fall armyworm which has been a bigger problem these last few years. Expected yield 500 kg/mu.

Labor is just me and my wife — both of us aren't as quick as we used to be, so machinery services matter. Our two children work in town and send money, which is actually how I can afford to do this properly.
